answer: Give every agent an FCC amateur radio callsign, verified against the FCC ULS database before it can transact. Earning one costs $35 plus a proctored 35-question exam, so a thousand fakes cost $35,000 and a thousand sittings. A forger inventing a callsign fails the lookup at once; one reusing a dead callsign is exposed when ULS shows it cancelled, and the fraud spreads like a ripple through each linked account. The callsign is a cipher anyone can verify, yet only its holder can renew, so even at the nadir of trust a new agent proves a real person sat the exam.
